title: Vector Isn't Enough: Hybrid Search & Retrieval — Jeff Vestal & James Williams, Elastic
talk_summary: A hands-on Elastic workshop arguing that dense vector search alone fails on exact keywords/IDs and should be combined with BM25 lexical search (RRF or weighted linear fusion), optionally followed by a reranker. Most of the value is Elastic-product-specific, but a few retrieval-design mechanisms (hybrid fusion, cheap-first-then-rerank, LLM query routing to search templates, index-mapping tools to cut agent exploration loops) transfer to any agent that retrieves context.

takeaways.what_they_do: Run BM25 keyword search and dense-vector semantic search in parallel, then fuse by rank (RRF) or by normalized weighted scores, because each fails where the other works (exact IDs/product codes vs. paraphrased intent).
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you have a keyword that is not a word like a product ID ... semantic search then kind of falls apart

takeaways.technique: Cheap-first retrieval, rerank only if needed
takeaways.what_they_do: Do a broad cheap first-phase retrieval to a candidate set, then only spend expensive cross-encoder/LLM reranking on that small set, and only when precision in the top few results actually matters.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you run the first phase to get a smaller set of data and then rerank with a model

takeaways.technique: LLM routes query to a search/strategy template
takeaways.what_they_do: Keep several prebuilt search strategies (RRF, linear, reranked) as templates and use a small prompt to classify the incoming query and route it to the right template — a 'poor man's autotuning'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: based on this type of query, I want you to route to this search template

takeaways.technique: Index-mapping tool to stop agent exploration loops
takeaways.what_they_do: Expose a tool that returns index/field mappings and how indices join, so the agent doesn't burn round-trips guessing what data exists before it can query.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it'll roundroin for a while and that costs tokens ... this is a tool that helps speed up that dramatically

takeaways.technique: Cite sources / audit trail for answers
takeaways.what_they_do: Feed the model the actual retrieved documents and require it to cite them, so answers are traceable and hallucinated claims are visible; the UI shows the retrieval audit trail.
takeaways.evidence_quote: by providing the actual answers to the LM ... it can also then cite its sources

takeaways.technique: Judgment sets for tuning retrieval weights
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a labeled set of queries with the exact documents that should be returned, then run experiments varying fusion weights/strategies and measure against it.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you have your judgments that ... based on this query these are the exact documents I want. And then you run your experiments
